boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Kettering customs shaped by alternating school-and-work sections, a distinctive Robot Society initiation, orientation rituals, community service, and commencement giving.

cards.title: Live by the A/B Calendar
cards.subtitle: School and co-op trade places every term
cards.notes: Confirm your assigned section, then plan each year around two academic terms alternating with two employer-based co-op terms.
cards.short_summary: Kettering divides undergraduates into opposing rotations that alternate campus study and paid workplace experience throughout the year.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering students follow A- or B-section rotations: A-section studies in summer and winter, B-section in fall and spring, and each works during its off-school terms.
cards.source_title: Undergraduate Enrollment | Kettering University Academic Catalog
cards.access_notes: The assigned academic/work sequence is part of undergraduate enrollment; changes require prior University approval.

cards.title: Put On the Robot White Gloves
cards.subtitle: Purity rendered as initiation attire
cards.notes: When documenting an initiation, frame the white gloves with the rest of the Robot attire so their ceremonial context stays visible.
cards.short_summary: Robot Society initiates wear white gloves that the University says symbolize purity.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering identifies white gloves as official Robot Society attire and states that they symbolize purity.
cards.source_title: Kettering University Inducts New Robot Society Members
cards.access_notes: This attire belongs to selected Robot Society initiates; observe or photograph only with event permission.

cards.title: Tie On the Robot Red Bow
cards.subtitle: A leadership bloodline in formalwear
cards.notes: Look for the vivid bow tie during an authorized induction appearance; the University assigns it a specific leadership meaning.
cards.short_summary: A red bow tie gives Robot Society initiates one of their most immediately recognizable ceremonial markers.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering lists a red bow tie among official Robot Society attire and says it represents the bloodline of a leader.
cards.source_title: Kettering University Inducts New Robot Society Members
cards.access_notes: The bow tie is ceremonial attire for Robot Society initiates, not a general visitor activity.

cards.title: Carry the R-Topped Cane
cards.subtitle: Membership marked with a single letter
cards.notes: Photograph the lettered cane alongside its initiate when permitted; separating it from the ceremony removes its documented meaning.
cards.short_summary: Robot Society members carry a cane topped by an R as an explicit sign of membership.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering states that official Robot attire includes a cane topped with the letter R to signify Robot Society membership.
cards.source_title: Kettering University Inducts New Robot Society Members
cards.access_notes: The cane is an insignia carried by Robot Society initiates; do not handle ceremonial property without permission.

cards.title: Hear the Robots Arrive
cards.subtitle: Bells announce the initiates
cards.notes: Listen for the bells at an authorized initiation event, where their sound is intended to draw attention to the new Robots.
cards.short_summary: Bells incorporated into Robot attire audibly announce the Society’s initiates.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering says bells are worn as part of official Robot Society attire to draw attention to the initiates.
cards.source_title: Kettering University Inducts New Robot Society Members
cards.access_notes: Hearing the bells depends on access to an authorized Robot Society appearance or initiation.

cards.entity_name: Robot Society Signing of the Keys
cards.title: Sign the Robot Keys
cards.subtitle: An initiation record shared across generations
cards.notes: If invited to observe, watch for the Keys after the pledge; active and honorary Robots present add their signatures during initiation.
cards.short_summary: The Robot ceremony concludes its formal commitments by gathering members’ signatures on the Keys.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering states that Robot Society initiation includes certification, recitation of the Robot pledge, and signing of the Keys by all honorary and active Robots present.
cards.source_title: Kettering University Inducts New Robot Society Members
cards.access_notes: The signing is part of a selective Society initiation; attendance is not represented as open to the public.

cards.title: Start Kettering by Serving Flint
cards.subtitle: Orientation leaves campus for community projects
cards.notes: Check your orientation assignment, dress for hands-on work, and arrive ready for the specific neighborhood or nonprofit project listed.
cards.short_summary: New students begin their Kettering experience with an organized day of service in Flint neighborhoods and community organizations.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering says Service Saturday has been organized for more than a decade, occurs annually during July and October new-student orientation, and sends students to Flint-area service projects.
cards.source_title: Kettering Students Support Flint Community on Service Saturday
cards.access_notes: Participation is organized through new-student orientation; project locations and assignments vary by section and event.

cards.title: Meet Your Unit Through Competition
cards.subtitle: Friday of Move-In and Launch Weekend
cards.notes: Follow the orientation agenda and join your assigned unit for Friday’s Olympics; event details are distributed through the student program.
cards.short_summary: Kettering’s incoming class encounters a named Unit Olympics during its required launch weekend.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering’s current Move-In and Launch Weekend schedule lists Unit Olympics among Friday’s new-student orientation activities.
cards.access_notes: This activity is part of required Move-In and Launch Weekend programming for incoming students.

cards.title: Close Orientation at Bulldog Fest
cards.subtitle: Kettering’s student-organization fair
cards.notes: Walk the Sunday fair after reviewing the club list, then note meeting expectations before committing to an organization or team.
cards.short_summary: Bulldog Fest turns the final orientation day into a Kettering-specific introduction to student activities and organizations.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering’s current orientation schedule identifies Bulldog Fest as a student activities and organizations fair held during Sunday’s orientation wrap-up.
cards.access_notes: The fair is scheduled within incoming-student Move-In and Launch Weekend; consult the student agenda for location details.

cards.title: Graduate in a Teal-Blue Cord
cards.subtitle: A class-year gift worn at commencement
cards.notes: Use the official commencement giving link if you want the cord, and complete the stated class-year contribution before ceremony deadlines.
cards.short_summary: Graduates can mark a class-year scholarship gift with a teal-blue philanthropy cord worn at commencement.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering’s 2026 commencement page says graduates who contribute $20.26 to the Keep Me Kettering Scholarship Fund receive a teal-blue philanthropy cord to wear at commencement.
cards.access_notes: The cord is offered to 2026 graduates through the official senior-gift contribution; participation requires a donation.
